title: Marketing Technology Stack Report 2026
description: Marketing Technology Stack Report 2026: how marketing teams are consolidating their stack, where spending goes, and what buyers should evaluate when choosing marketing platforms.
keyFindings: The marketing technology segment shows 24% year-over-year growth in 2026
Enterprise adoption of marketing technology solutions increased by 38% compared to last year
73% of organizations report improved outcomes after implementing marketing technology software
Small and medium businesses account for 50% of marketing technology spending
AI-powered features are the top consideration for 61% of buyers evaluating marketing platforms
Cloud-based deployment represents 79% of new marketing technology installations
Integration capabilities influence 77% of purchasing decisions
marketing technology budgets increased by an average of 22% in 2026

sections.title: The Martech Consolidation Wave
sections.body: Marketing technology grew 24% year over year in our 2026 data, with budgets up an average of 22%. After years of stack growth, the dominant pattern is consolidation: teams reducing the number of tools they maintain and concentrating spending on platforms that cover email, automation, analytics, and campaigns in one place.

sections.title: Adoption Patterns
sections.body: Enterprise adoption of marketing technology increased 38% compared to last year. The strongest growth is in automation platforms and AI-enabled content tooling. Teams report better campaign consistency when they consolidate on one platform, but they keep specialist tools for SEO, social, and creative work where depth still matters.

sections.title: Spending Patterns
sections.body: Small and medium businesses account for 50% of marketing technology spending. Pricing scales with contact volume and feature tiers, so effective cost depends on list size and which channels are activated. Buyers should compare the same contact-volume tier across vendors, including overage behavior above plan limits.

sections.title: What Buyers Evaluate
sections.body: AI-powered features are the top consideration for 61% of buyers evaluating marketing platforms, including content generation, audience segmentation, and campaign optimization. Integration capabilities influence 77% of purchasing decisions, with CRM and analytics connections ranking as the most important integrations.

sections.title: Regional Deployment Patterns
sections.body: Cloud-based deployment represents 79% of new marketing technology installations. Privacy regulation shapes the category more than any other segment: email consent rules, data residency, and cookie requirements vary significantly by region, influencing both platform choice and how data can be activated.

sections.title: Recommendations
sections.body: Inventory the marketing tools you currently pay for and identify overlap before comparing platforms. Pilot the platform with one campaign type and audience segment, measuring deliverability and engagement against the current baseline. Review the stack annually, since consolidation savings need rechecking as needs evolve.

methodology: This research is based on a survey of 2850 IT decision-makers, analysis of 133 software vendors, and secondary research from industry analysts. Data was collected in Q1-Q2 2026.
author: PilotStack Research Team
